newsitem.title: USA: FAA orders changes in Boeing 777 switches.
newsitem.headline: FAA orders changes in Boeing 777 switches.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has ordered operators of Boeing Co 777 jets to replace certain switches after several reports of false fire alarms and other problems.

In an emergency directive effective October 25, the agency warned that failure to comply "could result in inability of the flight crew to activate the cargo fire-extinguishing, fuel, air-conditioning and alternate flap systems."
The order comes after several false fire alarms apparently triggered by moisture given off by cargo including live frogs and tropical fruit.
In one case, more than a dozen passengers were injured when a Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd airliner was evacuated after a false fire warning.
The FAA said that in another incident one of the two cargo fire-extinguishing systems failed to discharge after the crew received what turned out to be a false fire alarm.
The fire-extinguishing system apparently failed because of a defect in a type of switch also used in the fuel, air-conditioning, and alternate flaps systems, the FAA said.
The agency ordered the airlines to replace the defective switches with new models made of a more resilient plastic.

A Boeing spokeswoman said the order affected 10 flight deck switches on all of the big twin-engine jets delivered so far. As of last week, 38 had been delivered since May 1995, and another 244 were on order.
The spokeswoman, Kirsti Dunn, said the FAA was looking into additional flight-deck switches and considering possible further action.

She said Boeing has come up with a way to prevent further false cargo fire alarms and issued a service bulletin instructing carriers to retrofit 777s with a device to improve the optical smoke sensor system.
